newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cemig sees record quarter in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cemig sees record quarter in Q3.

text.p: Brazil's state power firm Cemig will post its best quarterly results ever in the third quarter, buoyed by growth in the electricity market and higher tariffs, an official said.
"It will be our best quarter historically," Cemig's Assistant Finance Director Luiz Fernando Rolla said in an interview.
Minas Gerais is busy streamlining the giant state firm to prepare for greater competition as most of Brazil's power sector is sold off to private hands in coming years.
But unlike sweeping selloffs planned for the federally owned Eletrobras system and Sao Paulo state's energy firms, Minas Gerais state plans to shed only 33 percent of Cemig's ordinary voting shares.
"The state government decided Cemig was a strategic asset and did not want to relinquish control," Rolla said.
Rolla, who declined to predict third quarter earnings at the company owned by Minas Gerais state, cited projected market growth of six percent this year over 1995 as a main reason for optimisim.
Considered Brazil's lowest-cost electricity producer and one of its leading power firms, Cemig posted first-half earnings of 116 million reais, up 99 percent over the same period last year.
In addition to higher sales and electricity rates, the firm's third-quarter results will also benefit from improved efficiency, he said.
The 33 percent stake was put up by the state last year to secure a 430 million-real National Development Bank (BNDES) loan.
The state plans to sell the shares in a single block before October 31, the date the loan matures, to a "strategic partner" that will provide Cemig with new technology and fresh cash.
Minas Gerais, which will carry out a prequalification process, has already negotiated with several interested foreign investors.
Firms eyeing the one-third chunk of Cemig include Southern Electric Plc, Enron Corp, Chile's Enersis SA, Ontario Hydro and Hydro Quebec of Canada, EDF of France and EDP of Portugal.
No selloff model or base price have been established yet. But company officials said the state hopes to rake in 1.2 billion reais from the sale, roughly 60 reais a share.

Cemig, whose book value is 11.8 billion reais, is Brazil's cheapest electricity producer with an operating cost of 44.60 reais per megawatt hour, compared with 72.54 reais for Eletropaulo, 54.58 reais for Copel CPL_p.SA and 62.36 reais for Light, according to Cemig figures.

Rolla said the firm will invest about $500 million over the next four years to expand its customer base by 200,000 a year, extend transmission lines by 500 kilometers a year and build new generating units.
The company also is pushing ahead with cost-cutting measures, including slashing its payroll from 15,452 workers in June to 13,000 in 1999, he added.
